get.summary: Get one device model with its variants
get.description:
Fetches a single model from the device table selected by deviceType (Mobile, Tablet, Laptop, Desktop or Mac), including its class data. When the model is a parent (isParent = 1) and the type is not Laptop, its storage-ordered child variants are returned too.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. deviceType selects the underlying Prisma table, so the same id in different tables returns different rows.

_Source: `app/api/models/[id]/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

put.description:
Updates a model row in the table chosen by deviceType. The payload is zod-validated and then filtered against a per-device-type allow-list of columns, so unsupported fields are silently stripped rather than reaching Prisma.

**Notes:** Affects customer-facing quoted prices. Fields outside the per-device allow-list are dropped without error, so a silently ignored field is possible. No handler-level auth check (withAuditLog only records); middleware enforces the session.

**Notes:** Irreversible and can remove many rows at once (deleteVariants deletes every isParent=0 row with the same brand and model). No handler-level auth check (withAuditLog only logs).

SuccessErrorDetailsEnvelope.description: Error envelope `{ success: false, error, details }` where `details` is a string.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Plain error envelope `{ error }` used by most routes. `error` is a human-readable message.

deviceType.description: Device type the row belongs to

SuccessErrorDetailsListEnvelope.description: Validation error envelope `{ success: false, error, details[] }`.

status.description: One of pending | reviewed | added | rejected

processor.description: Processor name, e.g. Intel Core i7

value.description: Pricing value used by the laptop price engine

specs.description: Free-text specs used in the copy

isVariant.description: Generate variant-level copy; defaults to false

deviceType.description: Mobile | Tablet | Laptop | Mac | Desktop | Console | Camera | Headphone | Watch

model.description: Model name; required for every catalog that has the column

classId.description: Pricing class id; required for device types whose table has NOT NULL classId

deviceType.description: Mobile | Tablet | Laptop | Mac | Desktop - selects the table and the allowed column set

alt.description: Image alt text (not allowed for Desktop)

baseURL.description: URL slug base (not allowed for Desktop)

modelCode.description: Internal model code (not allowed for Desktop)

isParent.description: 0 or 1 - whether this row is the parent of storage variants

MessageEnvelope.description: Message-only envelope `{ message }`; used for both success and failure responses.

SuccessMessageEnvelope.description: Envelope `{ success, message }`; `success` is `true` on 2xx and `false` on error responses.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthenticated - no valid admin session (NextAuth cookie), or the expected token/secret is missing or wrong. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

cookieAuth.name: next-auth.session-token
cookieAuth.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie from logging in to the admin panel. On HTTPS the cookie name is `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

cronBearer.description: `LINODE_CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token — every cron job goes through `assertCronAuth` in `lib/linode/cron-auth.ts`, which reads only this variable (despite some jobs being non-Linode).

unverifiedAccessToken.name: Authorization
unverifiedAccessToken.description: Legacy customer routes: an `accessToken` cookie or an `Authorization` header must be PRESENT, but the value is never verified. Not real authentication.

adsWebhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
adsWebhookSecret.description: `ADS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, sent either as the `x-webhook-secret` header or as a `secret` field in the JSON body. If the env var is unset the route rejects every call with 401 (it does not fall through to unauthenticated access).

webhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
webhookSecret.description: Generic `x-webhook-secret` header check for an inbound webhook.

cronSecretBearer.description: `CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token, compared with `bearerMatches` in `lib/auth/secret-compare.ts`. Distinct from `cronBearer`, which uses `LINODE_CRON_SECRET`.
